name: Orthopyroxene
setting: Pbca (structural, a doubled; Dana (hkl) → (2k, h, l))

matrix.title: Prism cross-section × elongation
matrix.subtitle: Prismatic along [001], terminated by the dipyramids {211} and {111}. Columns change the cross-section from square to octagonal, rhombic and tabular.
matrix.note: Indices are structural Pbca. Dana's morphological axes have a<sub>D</sub> = b, b<sub>D</sub> = a/2, so Dana's (hkl) is (2k, h, l) here, and his letters a and b point at structural (010) and (100). Eight interfacial angles match Dana to within 0.25°. Which terminations dominate is poorly documented.

about: Orthopyroxene phenocrysts are prismatic along [001] with a characteristic eight-sided basal section built from {100}, {010} and the {210} cleavage prism, whose faces meet at about 88°. Hypersthene is often tabular on (010). Orthopyroxene is used for Fe–Mg diffusion chronometry of magma storage and ascent (Allan et al. 2013; Dohmen et al. 2016). Its 3D shape controls how a thin section samples the zoning.

habits.name: Octagonal prism
habits.text: {100} + {010} + {210}, the standard basal section of volcanic orthopyroxene (column o).

habits.name: Tabular on (010)
habits.text: Dana: hypersthene is often tabular parallel to (010) in the structural cell (column b).

habits.name: Acicular
habits.text: Rosettes of needles along [001] from fast growth (row L8).

references.citation: Nestola, F., Gatta, G.D., Boffa Ballaran, T. (2006). The effect of Ca substitution on the elastic and structural behavior of orthoenstatite. American Mineralogist 91, 809–815.
Dohmen, R., ter Heege, J.H., Becker, H.-W., Chakraborty, S. (2016). Fe-Mg interdiffusion in orthopyroxene. American Mineralogist 101, 2210–2221.

Allan, A.S.R., Morgan, D.J., Wilson, C.J.N., Millet, M.-A. (2013). From mush to eruption in centuries: assembly of the super-sized Oruanui magma body. Contributions to Mineralogy and Petrology 166, 143–164.
